incident_description:
I'm writing regarding the APOKE 3 in 1 Hair Dryer Brush & Straightener Brush on Amazon at [REDACTED].

This product is a fire/burn hazard and claims UL certification when I don't believe it's actually certified. I use this product to blow dry and straighten my hair at the same time (reduces frizziness). I have not experienced any fire or injuries.

I am copy/pasting my [REDACTED] below.
---
Lot of twists and turns here, so bear with me!

Original review: Great product, I wish a reliable company made it. Used it twice, then I kept hearing a staticky sound. I believe it has a short in it. I was already on the fence because this is an unknown brand and there is NO thingy on the end of the cord. The sound only happens when I plug it in, so in the trash it goes.

UPDATE: I was sent a replacement...which is clearly used. It was not in the wrapper, and the cords did not have twist ties (the cord was sort of wrapped around the barrel). Ew.

UPDATE UPDATE: I was asked by the company if I used the used one, and if so, did it work? Who uses a used beauty product?! That's disgusting, and I told them this. They sent a replacement...which also makes the staticky sound.

UPDATE UPDATE UPDATE: The sparking sound defect is happening in the replacement's replacement. I know what's going on. It's related to something I mentioned in the original review because I thought it very strange when I pulled the dryer out of the box. If you look, you'll notice it, too.

*This hair dryer has no external ALCI.* ALCI stands for Appliance Leakage Circuit Interrupter, and it's what saves lives when an appliance is dropped in water for example. It's the little box on the plug with the "test" and "reset" buttons! It senses a problem with the circuit - moisture, a fault in the product, or a fault with the outlet - and shuts off the product. This dryer does not have the UL symbol because UL requires *all* hair dryers to have an ALCI to obtain certification.

This is why the dryer makes the staticky/sparking sound (like static electricity discharging) or just stops working. It has a fault, and when it recognizes it and shuts off, you can't push the little button and reset it yourself. On functional versions of this product, you may be fine the first 24 power cycles or so, but then you'll hear the staticky sound and a click not long after that. The sound stops after the click. That's the internal mechanism doing its job. Sometimes the product shuts off and does *not* fix itself, but that's somebody else's review.

On my first dryer, there was no click, ever. I'd plug it back in, the sparking sound began again. On the replacement, the click worked correctly. I'd plug it back in, and no sparking sound. This is supposed to happen every time, but it doesn't.

This is why *external* ALCIs are the norm.

This company (or its supplier) tried to cut costs, and they're gonna burn down your house instead. They made a defective product and put in their own defective safeguards to stop you from noticing until you are outside of the 90 day return window. Or they made a product to sell cheaply and intentionally did not include an ALCI so that you would just buy another one when it quickly fails. Either way, very shady and I'm looking into product recalls.

If it makes noise, but you still use it because your budget and options are limited, please be careful and unplug it after EVERY use. Please.
justification: The product has a defect that poses a fire/burn hazard, but no actual incidents or injuries have been reported by the user.

incident_description:
MANSCAPED sells The Handyman Compact Face Shaver.
It is described as "Portable Mens Travel Facial Hair Groomer, USB-C Rechargeable Electric Razor, Waterproof, Cordless, Dual-Action SkinSafe Long-Hair Leveler & Foil Blades".
It is available not only alone, but as a bundle kit other accessories in different combo models.

This device almost caught fire or did catch fire in a smoldering manner, releasing toxic plastic fumes throughout the home to which people were exposed. A fire was very possible if there was any combustible material nearby, especially if the would-be-fire had not been caught early by someone with a good sense of smell. Those who are not able to locate or infer the sources of smells may be more at risk of death, property damage, or homelessness by fire.

The product comprises a USB-C charging cable, USB-C male charger wall outlet adapter, and the handheld product itself comprising of a grippable rechargeable battery sub-unit (and a cutter-and-foil-shaver sub-unit). While charging with the provided adapter (which has the same voltage and current markings as the battery unit), the battery unit overheated drastically, and over the course of half an hour leaked plastic fumes throughout the building. The product had disintegrated and melted on the battery unit where the USB-C cable connects to the charging circuitry. Charging port had reached sufficient heat that the plastic had melted onto the cable. At this temperature, we do not know if the lithium ion batteries may have been at risk themselves of catching fire.

A previous purchase of this product had sporadically-malfunctioning charging, so one can only surmise that the issue is systemic with this model, and perhaps with the manufacturer that MANSCAPED is working with in China, and related charging circuitry of related products.
justification: The incident involved a device that overheated and released toxic fumes, posing a risk of fire and potential injury or death, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Bleame crystal hair eraser online a few months ago. The website says it works with gentle pressure. I tried it out, and couldn't get it to work using gentle pressure, so I set it aside. A couple weeks ago, I decided to try it again, this time using more pressure. I was able to get it to remove hair using more pressure, I tried various techniques (on dry skin, wet skin,  and with shaving cream) as directed on the package, and I ended up with really bad skin irritation on my right arm. I also got milder skin irritation and rash on my left arm and inner thigh. The skin irritation occurred when I used the product as directed on their package and website, I documented my rash. I did not get skin burns from using the product on my lower legs, but I did get burns on my arms and inner thigh. I did some looking around online and discovered that I am not the only person who has had skin irritation/friction burns from this product and similar products. Severe skin irritation is a common complaint with people who use these crystal hair erasers. The "crystal" is actually etched glass similar to a glass nail file and it's like sandpapering your skin, especially when used on wet skin, which they recommend. The Bleame company does not warn people of the high potential for skin irritation with their product and actually touts their product as 100% pain free (I have already filed a complaint with the FTC concerning their deceptive business practices).
justification: The incident resulted in skin irritation and burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Online reports indicate this is a common issue, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description: I was using the BabylissProTT hair dryer to dry my 7 year old niece hair when the back of the blow dryer where the fan and motor is blew up crack the shell hit my face and started to smoke. I quickly unplugged the dryer. My niece was scared and started to cry. I never had a blow dryer do this it was very scary. This should be posted and the dryer removed from the shelves.
justification: The incident involved a blow dryer exploding and cracking its shell, causing smoke and scaring the child, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I have an eyelash curler which broke while in use sending a piece of metal into  the air.  Could have gone into my eye but landed on the countertop.
justification: The incident involved a broken eyelash curler but no actual injury occurred.

I can be reached at my e-mail address: [REDACTED]

Thank you.

incident_description: I am reporting this hot hair brush/ blow dryer brush because I noticed the brush getting extremely hot on one side, then I noticed that the pink plastic on the same side started to become disfigured. It looks as though the plastic melted and became disfigured because of the heat. I used the product once daily to style my hair and I immediately stopped using the product when the brush got too hot for me to hold so I would not get burned and I noticed the melting plastic.
justification: The brush became extremely hot and melted plastic, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Hair Dryer cord caught fire while using
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Revlon branded curling iron bearing an ETL test mark about 30 days ago from Amazon.  I have used the curling iron once a day for most days of the week.  Earlier this week, I plugged in and turned on the curling iron and was stunned to see the plastic tip fall off, smoke start coming out the exposed end, and one of the sets of combs along the side start to rise due to the heat.  I unplugged the curling iron and moved it outdoors.

Revlon stated that the curling iron comes from Helen of Troy in El Paso, TX.  The curling iron is marked as:
- Model: RVIR1054
- Type: RC1054AP
- Rating: 120V/240V, 60/50Hz, 80W Helen of Troy
- Intertek: 3095900
- Conforms to ANSI/UL Std 859
- Made in China

Although there were no injuries or property damage in this case, I can see where a recurrence might result in injury or property damage.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning curling iron with potential for injury, but no actual injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
I was using my Revlon 1875 hairdryer this morning. I noticed it wasn't blowing very hot on the low fan speed. When I turned it up to the higher speed, an explosion occured in the handle - and a flame and smoke shot out it - and the dryer turned off. 

I immediately unplugged the device - but I have to say it was extremely scary because the flame  that discharged from the handle was very close to my hair and face. My teenage daughter has the same model of hairdryer, so I am concerned that this is a dangerous product.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion and flame near the user's face, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I WAS BLOWDRYING MY HAIR AND SPARKS AND A FLAME SHOT OUT OF THE DRYER ALMOST BURNING MY HAIR AND SETTING OFF THE SMOKE ALARM IN MY HOME.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a flame from the blowdryer, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: HHP-375H model Handheld Dual Node Percussion Massager with Heat. I had this massager plugged in to the wall socket and was using it on my right knee. This was perhaps the 4th or 5th time I had used the product. Suddenly there was a loud crackling noise and a spark from the area where the cord attaches to the massager. It startled me and as I was trying to maneuver my hand so I could shut it off, the same area sparked again even more violently and smoke came from the handle. Fortunately, it tripped the circuit breaker which shut off the massager. The cord actually came apart at the joint to the handle and was completely severed. I was not injured, however I usually use the massager in bed which could have been a disaster.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and cord damage but no injury, and the likelihood is possible given it occurred after several uses.

incident_description:
While my wife was blow drying her hair, the cord closest to the plug burst into flames and caused a significant power surge throughout my home. My wife quickly dropped the hair dryer fearing from the fire and electrocution and ran out of the bathroom. As I approached the bathroom, the dryer was still smoldering, however no active fire. I went outside to my circuit breaker and turned off the power. I then proceeded to unplug the device.  

There was soot marks on the bathroom wall, and pieces of the cord on the counter top. There was no extension of fire into my wall from the plug and no other damage other than the wall.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and power surge, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I was blowdrying my hair for about 20 seconds.  I suddenly saw what i thought was a spark at the cord where it goes into the blowdryer.  I pulled the still running dryer away from  my hair and  then it started to flame.  I dropped it into the sink while it was still running.  I pulled the plug out of the wall and the flame recessed into the cord.
justification: The incident involved a spark and flame from a blowdryer, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My Chi Elite hair straightener caught fire this morning. I plugged it into the only outlet I have in my bathroom, which is located across the room from the sink, to allow it to warm up while I got dressed for the day. In the time it took me to get my underwear and socks on, I heard a series of loud pops emit from my straightener. When I looked over, small flames were coming out of it. I ran across the room (takes only 5 steps to do so) and unplugged it from the outlet, which seemed to stop the popping noise. There was a distinct electrical smell to it that lingered after I unplugged the straightener. The entire ordeal only lasted maybe 10-15 seconds, and at least I wasnt using the item when this happened.
justification: The hair straightener caught fire but was quickly unplugged without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: I purchased a Dyson hair dryer through a seller on eBay. The seller shipped the item and soon after the listing was removed due to violating policy. When I received the item, it worked at first and then all of a sudden got really hot, began to smell like it was burning, stopped working, with only lights flashing but no hair drying power. I then began researching and the item is counterfeit, and has a plug that is not allowed in the United States. It has a two-prong plug but no reset/test red and yellow buttons that are required. I reached out to Dyson and received official confirmation that the item is counterfeit. However, eBay wants me to return the item to the seller after knowing the item is counterfeit. eBay is encouraging the transportation of a counterfeit good through the United States Mail and does not seem to care that the counterfeit item is going to end up in the hands of the same seller who sold the counterfeit item in the first place. I am not sure if this is the correct place to report this, but please direct me to the right place if it is not.
justification: The counterfeit hair dryer malfunctioned but did not cause injury, and the likelihood of such incidents depends on counterfeit product availability.

incident_description: I had purchased a Revlon one-step dry and volume hair dryer and styler from Bed Bath and Beyond. The very first time I used it (less then a minute) I received an electric shock, heard a pop noise and the unit began to get very hot and smoke.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock and smoke, indicating a potential injury risk.

incident_description: I was drying my hair with this all in one drying/styling brush when it started to making popping sounds and the power of the unit started revving and lagging. I checked to be sure it wasn't overheated, and after a minute, turned it on and continued to dry my hair. The unit popped a few more times, then actually sparked. Several sparks flew into my hair and the air around me.  I immediately turned it off and unplugged it. Luckily my hair and skin were not injured. I simply wanted to file this report in case this isn't a one time incident. I'm worried someone might get hurt.
justification: The incident involved sparks but no injury, indicating a potential hazard.

incident_description: Female employee of our office was using the hand-held hair dryer when it began to produce sparks.  There was no fire, however the employee feels it may present a fire and/or electric shock hazard.  Upon examination, it appears the wiring is down to bare wires in one location on the electrical cord.  This hair dryer is a "cord keeper" hair dryer whereby the cord retracts into the unit.
justification: The hair dryer produced sparks but caused no injury or fire, indicating an incident without harm. The exposed wiring suggests a possible hazard if not addressed.

incident_description: Unattended massage gun (not charging) experienced catastrophic failure of li-ion battery and caused a fire in the kitchen of a townhome.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a battery failure, but no injuries or deaths were mentioned.

incident_description: Bleames crystal hair removal product causes dangerous and painful wounds that can lead to staph infections and long term issues. I tried their product and got painful rashes on my legs. I requested a refund, but I still have not received one.
justification: The description reports painful rashes and potential for staph infections, indicating injury.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that his wife plugged in and turned on her drying brush and right before she was about to use it flames started shooting out of it about six inches high. The consumers wife immediately turned off and unplug the unit and put it in water as it was still shooting flames. 

The consumer states that his wife uses the unit at least once per week for about ten minutes each use. 

The consumer plans on keeping the drying brush for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: Flames shooting out of the drying brush poses a significant fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On Saturday, January 28, 2023 at approximately 10:30 a.m., I unplugged my Conair 1875 hairdryer from the outlet and next thing I remember - I was flat on my back and had blacked out for a few seconds......I didn't know what happened.  I thought maybe when I bent over to unplug it - I thought maybe I got light-headed and passed out.  I have never passed out before in my life (I am 57 years old).  Later in the evening - I was getting ready to go out and again I plugged in my hair dryer (I use it to heat up my eyelash curler) and this time when I went to unplug it - I squatted down so that I didn't lean over and pull the plug out.  Next thing I know - i was on my back again and I had blacked out for a few seconds.  My 85-year old mother and my sister both heard me fall on the floor....at that time - I still didn't know what happened.  Then I realized that I had blacked out and fallen both times that day at the exact same time that I was unplugging that hairdryer.  I had an electrician come out on January 30th and he said there wasn't anything wrong with the actual outlet and it had to be the hairdryer plug that was the problem.  I have a black eye from the fall (I don't know if the black eye is from me pulling the plug out and possibly hitting myself in the eye when I got electrocuted or I don't know if the electrical current went in through my eye.  All I know is that it was a scary situation and I am worried about my heart.  I already have a rapid heart beat (supraventricular tachycardia) and I am lucky that I didn't actually die from being shocked twice in one day.
justification: The incident resulted in a black eye and temporary loss of consciousness, indicating an injury.

incident_description: One side of the cord broke at the base of the handle.caused arching and tripped the breaker. About two years old. Conair md259
justification: The cord breaking caused arcing and tripped the breaker, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: On the night of May 25th, I was beginning to straighten my hair with the Red by Kiss 1" ceramic flat iron. Everything was fine I made sure my area was dry and that my hair as well as my hands were dry. The product heated up fine but as soon after I began to straighten my hair the product began to audibly pop. I could not let the item go or remove it from my head due to the fact that I was being electrocuted by the current coming from the iron. It wasn't until the cord blew out of the back that I was able to put down the iron itself. From there I had to unplug the cord from the socket to prevent further damage. I have medical records, pictures, as well as the faulty appliance as evidence.
justification: The description indicates the person was electrocuted by the flat iron, which is an injury-causing incident.

incident_description: I took my 3 year 10 month old boy to the playground.  It was sunny, so I put his sunglasses on.  He tripped and fell forward.  The inside of the rim of the sunglasses cut him all the way through on the right side of his left eyebrow.  The wound required three sutures.  He is also bruised around the left eye in the same footprint as the rim of the sunglasses.  I examined the sunglasses and the inner rim that goes over the bridge of the nose is rather pointy and hard.
justification: The child sustained a cut requiring sutures and bruising from the sunglasses, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Conair massage wand unit that evidently has a heating device in it.  The switch to the heating device is not labled very well, and is not a switch, but a piece you turn on the wand.It looks like it is just part of the handle.  I never even knew the device was capable of heat.  The switch was turned on by accident, and must have been faulty for it became so hot as to give me a second and third degree burn on my leg.
justification: The incident resulted in second and third degree burns, indicating an injury.

incident_description: The item is a pair of baby nail clippers.  The piece that holds the handle to the clippers broke off whilst clipping my 3 month old son's nails.  It flung off mid-cut and flew across the room, hitting the opposite wall.  If it had flown any other direction, it could have hit either my son, or myself in the eye, or face.  It is very dangerous!
justification: The incident involved a broken nail clipper that flew across the room but caused no injury, though it had potential to cause harm.

incident_description:
I was using my neck and back massager from snailax and it burned/got super hot. I didnt think much of it because I was running after my kids and turned it off but this morning when I woke up the area was more tender and when I looked I had a huge scorch mark on my back where the burn occurred.

This is the product and I had it placed along my lower back at the time of incident
https://a.co/d/elrTUhT
justification: The massager caused a burn injury, as evidenced by the scorch mark and tenderness.

incident_description: I was using a portable hair dryer at my home when the cord (near where it attaches to the dryer) suddenly caught fire, shooting a three to four inch flame and slightly burning my arm.
justification: The incident resulted in a slight burn injury from the hair dryer cord catching fire.

incident_description: Hairdryer abruptly stopped working. Sometimes the plug falls out of the sockets, so I made sure it was firmly in the socket. I bent over to continue blowing my hair dry, and the hairdryer arched. It burnt a hold through my shirt and burned my abdomen. The arch appear to come out of the bottom of the handle and through the top of the cord. Prior to the incident, I noticed the case appeared melted. I should have discontinued use at that point.
justification: The hairdryer caused a burn injury to the abdomen, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the prior signs of damage (melted case) and the user's continued use despite them.

incident_description: Wife recently purchased a Conair Curling Iron Model M120.  Using it yesterday, she brushed it up against her cheek and received a significant electrical shock.  I examined the unit this morning and found that the cord insulation is cracked exposing both electical conductors where the cord enters the swivel mount for the cord.   This appears to pose a significant safety hazard to those using the device as well as the possibility of a fire.  The device says it is UL Listed.  Photos of the device and the cracked cord are available as is the device itself.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant electrical shock (injury) due to exposed electrical conductors, and the defect poses a continued hazard.

incident_description: Wife was using hair dryer that got very hot and began to smell.  She let it cool and set it down.  She then picked it up after 5-7 minutes and turned it on--it started to spark and shoot small flames.
justification: The hair dryer sparked and shot flames, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My 17 year old daughter was using the Rvdr5398 revlon brush/hairdryer in her room (not a bathroom) when the dryer changed pitch to a high whine and then sparked and shocked her. I unplugged it immediately. Her room smelled of smoke.
justification: The hairdryer sparked and shocked the user, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: Using blow dryer to dry wet hair (as usual) when 3" of sparks came out the back of the blow dryer (where the fan exhausts).  Dropped the blow dryer immediately eventhough it was still running and pulled plug from outlet.  Before turning unit off, upon impacting the floor, the sparks continued to emit and burned a 3" section of carpeting which was then extinguished with water.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a small fire but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Product was used by myself in accordance with all safety instructions. Was used on the genitals for several minutes, as the product was designed to be used. Personal lubrication was used which on previous usage by itself did not cause any problems. Product was used one time for 5 to 10 minutes with direct skin contact and rubbing on the penis, and then subsequently discarded. Immediately experienced cough, difficulty breathing, sick feeling in stomach, and headache. Symptoms continued for several days and worsened into sore throat, severe coughing, loose stools, and irritation of the penis, excessive urination, spontaneous constriction of genitals. Genitals coated with an oily chemical residue that is highly resistant to removal from the skin. This acute phase lasted for several weeks, and less severe symptoms persist after several months.

This is the third time I have used this product (in three years, each time purchasing a new one) and had nearly identical symptoms each time. Manufacturer insists it could not have been caused by their product. Urinalysis on two separate occasions showed no bacterial infection, but traces of blood in urine. Chemical composition of product is manufacturer secret, and they claim it's not made from latex or silicone, and that it's non-allergenic and phthalate-free. Allergist cannot confirm allergy due to unknown ingredients.

The majority of users of this product have not reported any similar problems. I believe in certain conditions this product is highly dangerous to human health, whether a person has an allergy, a person is genetically predisposed to having a sensitivity to the product, accidental misuse, errors in manufacturing, contaminated source materials used in manufacturing, or other unknown factors.
justification: The description details severe and persistent symptoms including injury and health issues, but no death. The majority of users report no problems, indicating the issue is rare for the general population.

incident_description: I had purchased a Conair Round Gel Grip Brush. While blowdrying my hair and using the round brush to straighten it; it came undone at the hadle. With the handle still in my hand, the round brush (that contains a rod in the middle) flew off and fell onto my left arm. It was extremely hot and it burned my arm. Luckily it wasn't my face and/or my children where not in the bathroom at the same time because it could have hit one of them.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the arm, but no further harm occurred.

incident_description: massage seat topper has damaged disc in my back
justification: The description states that the massage seat topper caused a damaged disc in the back, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: the hair dryer blow up in my little girl hand putting blisterd on her hand and shocking her i also have pics of her hand and the hair dryer some one needs to contact me aboout the matter or a lawyer will contact you i seen there was  a recall my dryer was not in the recall ty
justification: The hair dryer caused blisters and a shock, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I was microwaving the bear as instructed. The directions specifically said to microwave the Cozy Hugs brand panda bear in 30 second intervals up to 1 minute and 30 seconds in a rotating microwave. Such was done. I opened the microwave early upon noticing a burning smell and took the bear out, only to have many very hot ceramic beads spill onto my skin and cause minor burns from brief contact. Upon closer inspection, I noticed that a hole had been melted around the leg/hind end of the bear. The seams of the leg and hind end appeared to be damaged (possibly burnt) and had melted plastic (presumably from the faux fur fabric) all over the edges, with hot beads stuck in it. Hot beads spilled all over the floor and the bear, leaving them stuck to the exterior fabric and resulting in major risk of burns upon touching. Over half and hour later a smokey smell is still coming from the bear and the beads are still hot. The panda bear was bought new in package and I had used it a few times before (approximately 10 times total) since receiving it in January. There was no evidence of holes or tears before microwaving the bear.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns from hot ceramic beads, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the product failed under normal use conditions.

incident_description: My hairdryer burned me in the neck.  Something inside melted onto the coil and hot plastic shot out when I turned it on.  The plastic was the same color (hot pink) as the outside of the dryer.  It burned into my skin.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from hot plastic, indicating a clear injury.

incident_description: While the Aduro Massage Gun was plugged in and charging, it began to smoke. I was concerned it might ignite the carpet underneath, so I attempted to move it to a safer location. As I picked it up, it suddenly exploded in my hand.  This resulted in second-degree burns up my left arm, burns on my right arm, and damage to the carpet. I was rushed to the ER and also will need to follow up with the Burn clinic in a few days. The explosion was forceful and unexpected, and the device posed a serious fire and injury hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns and required emergency medical attention, indicating a severe injury.

incident_description: I am regularly cutting myself with a badly designed razor blade cartridge.  The cartridge has a precision trimmer that Harry's added in its remodel last year. In November 2016 I started using Harry's razors with the precision trimmer blade and began gashing myself with it whenever the blade handle slipped.  I have used similar cartridge designs from other makers, but have never had the problem that I am experiencing with these.  I noticed comments online from other customers with similar experiences using the same blades so that is why I am submitting this incident report.
justification: The description reports regular injuries (cuts) from the razor blade cartridge, and other customers have had similar experiences.

incident_description:
I am a female, age 48. I contacted BIC on September 2nd evening (See message in quotes below). I wanted to share an experience with you which has bothered me a lot due to the quality of the the BIC Soleil razor brand that I used. This was a brand new razor, I was shaving in the shower as I normally do. During normal usage, the razor top broke, exposing a blade that bent and caused a severe laceration on my lower calf. The resulting gash required 23 stitches, which resulted in an injury detailed below. I am also attaching photos for your team to look at.

Msg that was sent to BIC on Sept 2, 2017 via Contact Us page and via email shopbic@bicworld.com:

"On Sept 2, 2017 while shaving my legs with a BIC Soleil razor, at a normal pace during my shower, with no force whatsoever, the plastic
portion above the blade broke off, the blade popped out bent and ran through my skin as I moved the razor along my leg. A large chunk of flesh came out and there is a 25 cm long gash, lower portion where the flesh came out in a huge chunk. My leg was bleeding badly. I did not realize it until I saw the water turn red. I quickly stemmed the flow with a towel and tied it with a tourniquet, and rushed to the Emergency Room where they gave me local anesthesia, the wound required 23 stitches. I would like to bring this to the attention of the company. I have saved the razor and have photos of my wounds which I would like to send you. I don't have the packaging of the product or UPC code, since this was the last razor in my Soleil pack and I had already thrown out the packaging. My Contact no is XXX-XXX-XXXX.

This is not something small, a lifelong scar of 10 inches will remain and I would like to make you aware of this problem. I have to take time off from work on Tuesday to see my PCP for a dressing change (due to long weekend in the US, Labor Day holiday) and will know how the wound is healing. The ER physicians at Newton Wellesley Hospital, Newton, MA also suggested that I contact BIC to make sure that this is not a quality problem.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration requiring 23 stitches, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: I purchased your Homedics shiatsu body massager with heat.  After using it, I woke up with 2nd degree burns on my back that caused severe pain whereby the skin was burned from my back, sensitive exposed flesh, excruciating pain, inability to bathe, clothe, or maintain full attention to work each day.  I had lots of sleepless, crying nights due to the severe pain compounded by stinging burn wounds
justification: The description details severe 2nd degree burns and significant pain, indicating a serious injury.

incident_description: I wanted to report an extremely dangerous product so that what happened to me doesn't happen to anyone else. I purchased a curling iron (Rx7 Advanced Ionic Styling Tools) at Marshalls 6 months ago and have used it a few times as I have several different curling irons. On 6/27/24 as I was curling my hair, this curling iron caught on fire while my hair was in between the clamps. It started popping like fireworks with golf size balls of fire coming out of it. Fortunately, I was right beside my counter and was able to throw it down on my tile floor, unplug it, and was able to save my hair from major damage. I did receive a minor burn from where the wand hit my arm when I threw it on the floor. I was using the curling iron on dry hair as normal after it had warmed up about a minute.
justification: The curling iron caught fire and caused a minor burn, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: Two Projectiles from my BYRNA Pepper Spray Launcher somehow broke open while loaded into the accompanying Magazine and spread the contents (Pepper Spray material) all over the Handgun, the holster it was housed in and the side door compartment of my truck.  At a Stoplight just before arriving at my destination I removed the gun from the side door and set it on top of the Center Console so that I would not forget and leave the gun in my truck.  I have a Concealed Carry Permit.   After setting the gun down on the console I rubbed my upper right eyebrow to scratch an itch and immediately I was blinded by the Pepper Spray residue that I had apparently touched when moving the gun.  I was able to make the right turn at the light and pull over and from my military experience I knew immediately what the issue was and began flushing my eyes with Potable Water.  It took approx 10 minutes to get my vision back and stop the very painful burning sensation coming from the Pepper Spray residue.
justification: The incident involved pepper spray exposure causing temporary blindness and pain, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the described handling of contaminated equipment.

incident_description:
I obtained a large 2nd degree burn on my cheek while using the TIGI Bed Head Wave Affair 3 Barrel Digital
Jumbo Hair Waver to style my hair. I was using this product as intended. I followed the instructions in the
manual and read the full manual prior to its first use. The outside bottom of the plate that opens when you
press the handle to put your hair in for styling slightly touched my face for an 1/8 of a second and I now have
a very painful large oozing burn on my cheek. The product was so big it obscured my visibility in the mirror while styling my hair, and The product is extremely heavy for one hand use on the lever. Also there is no
protective covering for the outside of the plate that is the backside of the tool used in the styling of the hair, opens wide with push of the lever/
when you press the clamping lever. The manual does not mention the outside of the plate is as hot as the
barrels or as hot as the interior part of the product that does the styling.
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn, which qualifies as an injury. The likelihood is possible due to the product's design flaws and lack of warning about the hot exterior plate.

incident_description:
This product injured my right hand on May 2, 2018 when I first tested out the product after I had purchased it on 4/29/2018.  I pressed the button to retract the cord and the force of retraction is so strong that it whips up and the end (thick plug) will hit whatever is in it's way.  This could definitely hurt someone who isn't paying attention to their surroundings and injure themselves or someone that happened to be near them (for example a child).  This product injured me and I WAS PAYING ATTENTION, so this is why I am reporting this.  

The injury resulted in bruising and a tiny laceration on my right hand.
justification: The product caused bruising and a small laceration, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests the mechanism could easily harm others, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: On January 6th I was straightening my hair with my Con Air Infinity Pro hair straightener. I was sitting on the floor, with a blanket covering my legs. The heat setting was set to five out of of 30. I was almost done straughtening my hair. I was holding the straightner above my lap, when the iron made a big, bright spark, which looked like a 4th of July sparkler. It burned a hole through my blanket and burned my foot. The chord looks like it exploded on one side. Two days prior, on January 4th, I was straightening my hair and accidently touched my face. The burn seemed disproportionate to low setting (5). I currently have two nickel size burns on my lower cheek and jaw. It indicates the iron had stoppwd regulating the tempature atleast two days before the wire exoloded.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the foot and face, indicating injury (severity 3). The malfunction suggests possible recurrence if the device is not repaired or replaced (likelihood 3).

incident_description: This device heats up while massaging and the cover comes off.  The cover came off and burnt my back.
justification: The cover came off and caused a burn, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The curling iron had been in the on position for approximately 2 to 4 minutes and the consumer noticed that it had begun to emit smoke.  The consumer immediately turned the curling iron "off".  She looked at some of the literature that came with it and the paper indicated that some type of coating was applied to the iron and it would emit smoke the first time it was turned on, but would dissipate shortly.

The consumer turned the curling iron back on sometime later and it still emitted smoke.  However, the consumer was not concerned, because the literature had indicated that there was no need to be concerned.  Immediately after applying the iron to her hair, her hair turned red and then turned black.  The consumer turned the curling iron off and found that some of her hair had adhered to the iron.  

The hair loss occurred to the left, front portion of the consumer's hair.  No Rx. needed.  The hair dresser ended up cutting off the other burned/dry areas of hair that were affected by the curling iron and said that it would have to grow back over time (approximately 9 - 12 months).

The consumer called the mfr. and a rep. by the name of [REDACTED] (position unknown) called the consumer back from their Customer Service Dept.  They provided a shipping label and [REDACTED] asked the consumer how much she paid to have her hair done.  After the consumer told him, [REDACTED] agreed to send the consumer a check for compensation.  The consumer received a check for $75.00 from the firm.  The consumer mailed the curling iron back to the firm on March 2, 2011. 

The consumer received a return letter from the firm and it indicated that the curling iron was sent to their testing lab on 3/10/2011 and it would take 3 business weeks before the examination was complete.
justification: The incident resulted in hair damage requiring cutting and regrowth, but no medical treatment was needed.

incident_description: There is a company promoting magnetic headbands in my community. [REDACTED] The product name is Magneblooms and they are sold online at www.lehlashop.com. The headbands gave me a terrible headache when I wore them.
justification: The headbands caused a headache, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue was experienced by the user but broader occurrence is unclear.

incident_description:
I have owned several of the Home Medic percussion massagers over the years they were always fairly well made and lasted a long time, so I purchased another. The changes to the product this time were obvious and not impressive, you can tell by the lack of power and the effort to make the product lighter and cheaper, especially the smaller gauge power cord! But we went ahead and used it anyway because I just don't have time to hassle with stuff over the internet. What a joke, after maybe 6 total hours of use; I was using it on my shoulder, I heard a loud pop, saw sparks, felt a burn on my wrist, and heard my AC circuit breaker click off, in that order, almost simultaneously! 
     The burn on my arm was minor and gratefully because I engineered the AC electrical in my home better than the morons who engineered this massager, there was no damage to my system. The worse part is, what if it had been one of my kids or an elderly individual? What if it had caught something on fire?
     This kind of irresponsible thought process is what has and will continue to destroy everything good and descent. Some idiot sitting at a desk decides he needs to make more profit; "  lets give it a little smaller motor, or a smaller / lighter case ( the Millennial's will like it especially if it looks cooler ), oh and lets use 18 gauge power cable instead of 16 ( the most important part that carries juice to the whole thing! ) and of course to hell with the consequences because we make more money!"
     Well here's a thought process; in the past I have personally owned 13 Home Medics products and my extended family has and does own about 37 more. After this do you think we will ever buy anything else with that name on it?    

Concerned Customer and Electrical Engineer,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn (injury) and potential for more severe outcomes, with the product's design flaws increasing the likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: My 3 year old ingested a metal scunci hair clip.  The clip became lodged near her duodenum.  Attempts to recover the lodged clip noninvasively failed.  The clip was removed by open surgery, however the success of surgery was questioned and required the site to remain open under a wound vac overnight.  A second surgery the following day was not promising.  A leak continued to be suspected.  My child remained hospitalized for 19 days during the first admission due to a suspected leak at the surgical site.  Discharged after the suspected leak walled itself off.  About 4 weeks later my child was redmitted for 12 more days after 2 adhesions formed.  Open surgery was again conducted and appx 1 foot of intestine was removed.
justification: The child suffered severe injuries requiring multiple surgeries and extended hospitalization, but there was no mention of death.

incident_description:
A consumer placed the full hood professional hair dryer on a sofa for use.  The product was turned on and left unattended for a period of time.  Heat from the product caused the sofa to ingite.  Fire damaged the sofa and room of origin.

I purchased an exemplar of the product for my fire investigation.  The instruction manual clearly warns to never leave the dryer unattended and never to use on a bed or couch because the vents can be blocked.

The consumer was not injured.  The product was destroyed in the fire.  

Palm Beach County Fire Rescue case #[REDACTED].
justification: The incident caused fire damage to the sofa and room but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as misuse warnings were provided but not followed.

incident_description:
On Thanksgiving day I was electrocuted while unplugging my L'ANGE HAIR Le Volume 2-in-1 Titanium Brush Dryer  from the outlet. 
My hands were dry and the device was powered off at the time.

I was electrocuted in my left hand, up my left arm and into my chest. I immediately took myself to the ER.
At the ER, an EKG and a number of lab tests were performed. When my tests came back normal, I was discharged. 

The following day, I had an electrician to my home to inspect the outlet and the electricity within my home. He found nothing, and concluded that the device must be solely responsible for my being electrocuted. 

I am seeking reimbursement for the cost of the device, my hospital bills and the cost of the electrician visit. 

I notified the manufacturer of my complaint via the email form on their website on 11/27 and indicated that I would be filing a report with the CPSC
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring ER visit, but no long-term harm was detected.
